eligible.content: That's exactly what I was thinking—checking the top layer first makes the most sense. I just hope I don't forget to do it when I'm distracted by the heat.

No problem at all! Sometimes when things are hot, it’s easy to get distracted by the heat or the day’s schedule. Just try to set a quick reminder on your phone to check those pots twice a day. It should help keep you on track! Hope the heat doesn't cause too much stress for your plants!

sources.content: I think they're just heavy because the soil is packed tight—most of them are plastic. I'll try to water them more thoroughly this time, but I'm worried about overwatering in the heat.

It sounds like the soil is holding a lot of moisture right now, which is common with plastic pots. If you're worried about overwatering, try to monitor the soil moisture before watering them again—maybe just a gentle touch or a quick "squeeze test" on the top inch or so of soil to see if it still feels slightly damp. Better to be a bit on the light side than to have roots get waterlogged, which can cause rot!
I'll keep that in mind—maybe I'll check a couple more pots tomorrow before watering again. It's just tricky when the heat makes everything feel so dry on the surface.

Sounds like a smart approach! Monitoring the soil moisture directly is a good idea. Just remember to check the top layer first—if it still feels dry, that's your cue to water. Good luck with the monitoring! Let me know how it goes!
